statements.status_notes: django.utils.cache.has_vary_header() is consulted only by the response-cache middleware and the cache_page() decorator, which codecov-api never enables (no cache middleware in any settings module, no cache_page() caller in the application, the shared library or any third-party module), so whitespace-padded Vary values never reach a cache-key decision. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.15 and 6.0.6; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

The vulnerable code is UpdateCacheMiddleware and the cache_page() decorator. codecov-api never enables Django's response cache: no settings module lists UpdateCacheMiddleware, FetchFromCacheMiddleware or CacheMiddleware in MIDDLEWARE, and no application, shared-library or third-party module in the image calls cache_page(), so responses that vary on cookies are never written to a shared cache. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.16 and 6.0.7; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

codecov-api calls get_signed_cookie for exactly two cookies, _bb_oauth_state (codecov_auth/views/bitbucket.py) and _oauth_request_token (codecov_auth/views/bitbucket_server.py), both with the default empty salt, and no other application, shared-library, third-party or Django-internal code path in the image reads signed cookies (sessions use the cached_db engine). The flaw needs two signing contexts whose name+salt concatenations coincide; the only two contexts are distinct strings and an attacker cannot mint signatures without SECRET_KEY, so a cookie signed in one context is never accepted in the other. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.15 and 6.0.6; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

The vulnerable code is django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware. codecov-api never enables Django's response cache: no settings module lists UpdateCacheMiddleware, FetchFromCacheMiddleware or CacheMiddleware in MIDDLEWARE, and no application, shared-library or third-party module in the image calls cache_page(), so no response is ever stored in or served from the response cache regardless of its Cache-Control directives. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.15 and 6.0.6; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

DomainNameValidator was introduced in Django 5.1; the shipped Django 4.2.30 has no DomainNameValidator or validate_domain_name in django/core/validators.py, so the vulnerable code is not in the image. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.16 and 6.0.7; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

GeoDjango is not part of this image: django.contrib.gis is absent from INSTALLED_APPS in every codecov-api settings module, nothing in the application or the shared library imports it, and the image ships no GEOS or GDAL native library, so django.contrib.gis.gdal.GDALRaster cannot be constructed and its vsi_buffer property is never read. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.16 and 6.0.7; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.

GeoDjango is not part of this image: django.contrib.gis is absent from INSTALLED_APPS in every codecov-api settings module, nothing in the application or the shared library imports it, and the image ships no GEOS or GDAL native library, so django.contrib.gis.geos.GEOSGeometry, the spatial lookups and the GeometryField form field cannot be loaded, let alone reached with attacker-supplied WKT or WKB. Fixed upstream only in Django 5.2.17 and 6.0.8; Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 with 4.2.30 as its final release.
